newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY NOON RADIO HEADLINES - FEB 28.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY NOON RADIO HEADLINES - FEB 28.

text.p: These are the main headlines on Hungary's Kossuth Radio midday news. Reuters cannot vouch for their accuracy:

_ Chairman of Postabank denied rumours that the bank's financial standing had been shaken. Gabor Princz said that Postabank continued to be stable, the finance ministry and the state banking supervision were monitoring the bank and did not see any reason for clients' worries.

- More than 300 farmers gathered at Kiskoros in order to decide whether to accept the allowances offered by the government or to go on with the demonstrations started on Wednesday. One of th main organisers of the demonstration said farmers do not seem to be satisfied with the results achieved by the protest.

- The minister for agriculture does not see any more possibilities for further allowances to be offered to farmers and hopes that at the forum of farmers organised at Kiskoros today organisers will accept the government's proposal.

- Road transportation firms are dissatisfied. Their association will vote at today's general meeting on whether to start negotiations with the government about the improvement of conditions prevalent in the road transport sector.
- The police have detained the owner of the Soltvadkert-based chocolate plant because in one of the warehouses of the company a large quantity of metal-lined banknote paper has been found
- The police have found the murderer of the Chinese woman who was killed on Tuesday in the 8th district of Budapest. The murderer is also of Chinese nationality.
